prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” broker that fits everyone — the right one depends on your budget, health needs, and whether you want help only for ACA (individual) plans, short‑term coverage, an HSA‑eligible plan, or things like COBRA/Medicare. Rather than picking a name at random, I recommend a quick process to find a highly qualified broker in Kansas City who specializes in self‑employed people.

How to find the best broker for you
- Look for an independent agent/broker (not captive to one carrier) so you can compare multiple carriers.
- Confirm they’re licensed in Missouri — you can verify licenses with the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance.
- Ask whether they have experience with ACA/Marketplace plans, premium tax credits, HSAs, and small‑business solutions (if you want to set up a group alternative).
- Ask how they’re paid (commissions vs. fees) and whether any advice or quote comparisons are free.
- Ask for references or recent client reviews, and check Google/BBB reviews.
- Make sure they provide ongoing help (enrollment, plan changes, claims assistance) — that’s especially valuable for self‑employed people who need hands‑on guidance.

Places to look / resources
- Marketplace-certified navigators or brokers: they can enroll you in HealthCare.gov plans and explain subsidy eligibility.
- National broker directories: NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) has a local chapter directory where you can find credentialed agents in Kansas City.
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance: license lookup and consumer complaint records.
- Online broker platforms (e.g., eHealth, HealthSherpa): good for getting quick quotes across carriers, but you’ll miss personalized local support unless you ask for an agent.

Questions to ask any broker before you commit
- “Are you independent or contracted with specific carriers?”
- “How long have you worked with self‑employed clients?”
- “Which carriers and plan types do you compare?”
- “Do you help determine eligibility for premium tax credits and calculate net monthly cost?”
- “Will you help after enrollment if I have billing or claims problems?”
- “Do you charge me a fee, or are you paid by the insurer?”

If you want, I can:
- look up licensed individual brokers in Kansas City (I’ll need your ZIP code), or
- shortlist a few well‑reviewed local brokers/agencies that handle ACA/individual plans and self‑employment needs.

Which would you prefer?
